svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.15.4.3 Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.15 FOOTINGS AND FOUNDATIONS
Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top

g.text: Floor system anchored to the wall
Footing to not more than 300 mm
both sides, grades differ by not
Beneath an opening over 1.2 m wide:
Flat ICF wall: joists installed to
Joist hangers on a wood ledger

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Sentences (2) to (4) apply to the walls described in
Sentence 9.15.4.2.(1)
Foundation walls are laterally supported at the top if
(a) they support a solid masonry superstructure or flat ICF
wall, (b) the floor joists are embedded in the top of the
walls, (c) the floor system is anchored to the top of the
walls with anchor bolts, the joists running either parallel
or perpendicular to the walls, or (d) they extend from the
footing to no more than 300 mm (11 13/16″) above finished
ground level and are backfilled on both sides, the finished
ground levels differing by no more than 150 mm (5⅞″).
Unless the wall around an opening is reinforced to
withstand earth pressure, the portion beneath an opening
is laterally unsupported if
(a) the opening is more than 1.2 m (3′-11¼″) wide, or (b)
the total width of the openings is more than 25% of the
length of the wall.
Openings are taken as one opening where their average
width is greater than the width of solid wall between
them
Flat ICF foundation walls are laterally supported at the
top if the floor joists are installed to Article
Drawn: walls cut through, basement to the right. E: a 1.5 m opening, portion beneath in pink. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.15.4.3. (page 9-124), with Article 9.20.17.5.
